$comment: The ask-form FIELD TYPE and ANSWER CONSTRAINT rules, pinned across the two
languages that implement them — internal/askforms (definition validator, CLI)
and lib/ask-validate.ts (the sheet the user actually answers).
This is a second golden fixture, deliberately NOT testdata/ask-templates.json.
That one pins the two RENDERERS; nothing in here is a rendering rule, and
mixing them would mean a constraint change had to touch the file that keeps
A rule added on one side and not the other is a red run in both suites.
$rule: known  — this client has a control for it and renders that control.
open   — never heard of it, but the name is inert, so it renders as a text
input. This is what lets the server ship a field type without a
coordinated frontend release, and it is kept on purpose.
unsafe — a name that says the value is a secret, or a name shaped so that
nothing can be trusted to render it. It FAILS CLOSED: the
definition validator refuses to save it, and if one is already
stored (a row written before the validator, or edited around the
API) the sheet renders no input for it and refuses to submit.
The asymmetry is the point. An ask form renders into an ordinary, durable
chat message; there is no field type that makes that safe for a secret. So
the list stays open for types whose worst case is a plainer control, and is
closed exactly where the fallback would be a lie.

types.$why: a type this release has never heard of still renders — the open list
contains 'key' but is not the token 'key' — a substring match here would close the list on nonsense
a false positive we accept: 'token' anywhere in a type name fails closed, and the cost is one awkward rename
uppercase never reaches a control — the shape rule catches it before the sensitivity rule has to

$constraints: WHERE A CONSTRAINT MEANS WHAT. `min`/`max` are one pair of numbers in the
schema and three different questions depending on the field:
number, money            -> the VALUE must fall in range
text, textarea, open     -> the LENGTH in characters must fall in range
multiselect, file, photo -> the COUNT of answers must fall in range
`pattern` is anchored (the whole value must match) and applies only to the
text-ish types. `multiple: false` caps an upload field at one file.
Every combination not listed above is REFUSED WHEN THE FORM IS SAVED, which
is the same principle as the placeholder rule: a constraint the submit path
would not enforce must not be storable, or the author is told a lie about
An empty OPTIONAL answer is not a violation — only `required` speaks to
emptiness. Otherwise a form with `min: 3` could not be left blank.

answers.name: a required text field left empty names itself
an optional field left empty is not a violation of its own constraints
text min is a length

errors.message: Note must be at least 3 characters.

answers.name: text max is a length, and one character is singular

errors.message: Code must be at most 1 character.

answers.name: an answer is measured after its edges are trimmed, exactly as the renderer would send it
a length is counted in characters, not UTF-16 units
number min is a value
number max is a value
a number that is not a number says so before it says anything else
money is a number field with a currency beside it
a fractional bound keeps its decimals in the message
pattern is anchored — a match somewhere inside is not a match

errors.message: VAT ID is not in the expected format.

answers.name: pattern accepts the whole-value match
multiselect min is a count of choices
multiselect max is a count of choices
a choice that is not on the list is not an answer

errors.message: Category must be one of its listed options.

answers.name: an option carrying stray whitespace is still answerable
answers.$why: every answer is trimmed on its way through (see the '  ab  ' case above), so a raw option compared against a cleaned answer never matches: the form renders 'Travel', the user picks 'Travel', and the sheet refuses it while blaming their choice. Such a definition cannot be SAVED any more (Normalize trims the options), so this is the row that predates the rule — it has to stay answerable rather than fail closed, the same call the uncompilable-pattern case makes

answers.name: trimming the options does not widen them

errors.message: Category must be one of its listed options.

answers.name: a multiselect option carrying stray whitespace is answerable too
file min is a count of uploads
multiple:false is one file and says how to fix it

errors.message: Document takes one file — remove the extra ones.

answers.name: multiple:true is the default and allows several
a required upload field says to attach, not to type

answers.name: a field with no type at all is checked as the text input it renders as
answers.$why: the definition validator refuses a typeless field outright; this is an answer checked against a row that never met it, and failing closed there would blank a field that has always rendered fine

errors.message: Note must be at most 3 characters.

$definitions: Definition-time rejections, asserted by the Go validator only (the console
never writes a definition; it reads one). Listed here so the two sides
agree on WHICH definitions can reach a user at all.

definition_rejections.name: a secret-like type cannot be saved
a type nothing can render cannot be saved
a pattern that does not compile
a pattern on a type nothing matches it against
a bound on a date, which the submit path would not check
multiple on a field that is not an upload
two options that differ only by whitespace are the same option
definition_rejections.$why: the options are trimmed on write, so these two would be stored identically and render as the same choice twice — the duplicate check has to see them the way the user will
